sections.name: Tata Safari
lines: The Tata Safari name goes back to 1998, when it was one of India's first lifestyle SUVs.
The old Safari was a boxy, body on frame four by four.
In 2021 it was reborn as a modern monocoque SUV. It was previewed as the Buzzard concept at the 2019 Geneva motor show.
It rides on Tata's Omega Arc platform, derived from a Land Rover architecture.
The two litre diesel makes a hundred and seventy P S and three hundred and fifty newton metres, with manual or automatic.
The updated Safari scored five stars in both Global N CAP and Bharat N CAP crash tests.
Inside, a twelve point three inch screen, level two driver assistance, a panoramic sunroof, and optional captain seats.
A legendary name, now with seven seats, top safety, and huge road presence.
